Devika Mallik
Product Designer
London, UK · Portfolio · Linkedin
PROFILE
Product designer with 4 years delivering complex, multi-sided digital products across fintech, healthcare, and
experiential platforms. Moves with ease across interaction states and edge cases to compliance flows and system
architecture. Trained in Service Design and Systems Thinking at the Royal College of Art, with a background in
economics. Experienced designing in regulated, high-stakes environments where design decisions carry real
consequences.
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Product Strategy and UX Consultant | Vizara Technologies, India. 2021–2024
· Sole product designer delivering end-to-end design across 5+ digital platforms in government, cultural, and
immersive-tech contexts, taking products from research and concept through to shipped, developer-handed-off
builds. Worked within agile sprint cycles, setting design milestones, and collaborating directly with engineering
and product stakeholders.
· Increased walkthrough completion from under 5% to ~31% by replacing linear navigation with hotspot-based
exploration across 3 user segments; on a separate platform, increased content discovery from under 1% to ~13%.
· Shipped live products across government, institutional, and exhibition contexts; on a live AR exhibition product,
measured 6.1/7 satisfaction across 22 on-site users through structured testing.
· Conducted ethnographic fieldwork visiting artisans on-site to translate lived craft practice into navigable digital
experiences.
· Integrated engineering earlier in the design cycle, sat with developers during implementation including Unity UI
work, and structured developer handoff, cutting revision cycles by ~40% and late-stage rework by ~12%.
· Contributed UX strategy and design assets to a government portal concept delivered in 7 days, supporting a $4M
public-sector partnership opportunity.
Product Designer | Freelance, India, UK and International 2020–Present
· Independent product design for early-stage startups: built complete product foundations from partial briefs
(user flows, design systems, edge cases, error and empty states, monetisation), and advised pre-seed founders
on UX and AI interaction standards including source transparency and recommendation framing. Work
incorporated into client builds and investor materials.
SPONSORED AND PARTNER PROJECT
AI Product Design, EY Seren | EY Industry Partner Project 2024–2025
Led mixed-methods research to address gender bias and build trust in AI-driven financial products during high-stakes
financial moments.
· Designed a predictive AI financial companion for women that detects high-risk financial moments and
intervenes in real time, using behavioural and physiological signals without removing user agency.
· Grounded in 130+ surveys and 15+ interviews; identified trust breakdown points across onboarding friction,
unfamiliar-market anxiety, and gender-skewed assumptions.
· Developed a Trust Pyramid framework governing how AI earns credibility progressively; tested across three
intervention models, achieving a 60% increase in positive user feedback. Presented findings and product direction to
EY's design team.
Product Design, HealthTech Startup | Imperial College London 2024–2025
Led MVP scoping and patient-side product design for a dual-sided healthcare marketplace responding to NHS access
delays, connecting patients with verified GPs for same-day home visits in London.
· Solved the supply-side chicken-and-egg problem: GPs browse patient demand and build profiles before completing
verification, with bookings locked until medical credentials are manually approved.
· Designed two distinct patient onboarding entry modes within a single interface: emergency users browse and
book first with account creation deferred to payment; routine users onboard fully upfront.
· Owned GP compliance onboarding across three progressive stages, mapping documentation and regulatory
requirements sequentially to reduce abandonment without compromising compliance.
· Scoped the product from 30+ features to 12 across two structured prioritisation workshops, aligning founders,
clinical advisors, and engineering on MVP scope. Delivered build-ready MVP and developer-handoff specification,
validated through stakeholder review.
Service Design, Ministry of Defence | WICKED Acceleration Labs, Imperial College London2024–2025
Led systems mapping and business design methods to support the Royal Air Force's goal of reducing carbon emissions
and embedding Social Value provisions into procurement and delivery.
· Diagnosed the core failure as structural rather than financial: sustainability accountability sat between functions
with no clear ownership across the procurement chain.
· Designed a Social Value Activation Plan embedding sustainability outcomes into procurement decisionmaking at the point of design, co-developed with policy, procurement, and delivery stakeholders.
